title: Modi Calls Naidu as Andhra Counts Losses From Two Cyclones in a Week
excerpt: Andhra Pradesh has pegged preliminary Cyclone Murasu losses at Rs 343.95 crore and Cyclone Arnab losses at Rs 4,526 crore, and is pressing the Centre for assistance while a central team assesses drought in 388 mandals.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday morning to ask about damage from Cyclones Arnab and Murasu, which struck the state within a week of each other.
  • Cyclone Murasu alone caused a preliminary loss of Rs 343.95 crore across eight government departments, about 94 per cent of it in agriculture: crops over 50,473 hectares in 465 villages were damaged, affecting 69,828 farmers.
  • Naidu has also sought central help for drought: 388 mandals across 21 districts have been declared drought-affected, and an Inter-Ministerial Central Team that inspected four districts on November 2 and 3 will report to the Centre within 15 days.
  • No central assistance package has been announced yet. The assistance decision follows the central team assessment, so affected families should watch for the team report and the state memorandum process over the next two weeks.

Andhra Pradesh is counting the cost of two cyclones in seven days. Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday morning to enquire about the damage caused by Cyclones Arnab and Murasu, according to Telugu360. Naidu briefed him on agricultural and infrastructure losses from heavy rain and strong winds and requested central support for relief, rehabilitation and restoration work.

The damage, in numbers

Cyclone Murasu, the second storm, caused a preliminary loss of Rs 343.95 crore across eight government departments, with roughly 94 per cent of that in the agricultural sector, according to an official release reported by Nation Press. Crops spanning 50,473 hectares across 465 villages in seven districts were damaged, affecting 69,828 farmers. The earlier storm was costlier still: briefing a visiting central team on Monday, Naidu put preliminary Cyclone Arnab losses at at least Rs 4,526 crore, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. During the response, 11 State Disaster Response Force teams and 13 National Disaster Response Force teams were kept on standby, 480 schools were converted into relief centres and 12,230 people were evacuated to safer locations, according to Nation Press.

Naidu has also written to Union Home Minister Amit Shah urging the Centre to release immediate financial assistance, and Shah had separately called Naidu twice on Tuesday to assess the cumulative damage from both cyclones, according to Nation Press. Modi, for his part, praised the state government relief operations during the call. No disbursement has been announced.

A drought layered on top of the storms

The cyclone appeal is only half of the state case to New Delhi. Naidu also met the Inter-Ministerial Central Team that inspected drought-affected areas in Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts on November 2 and 3. He told the team that 388 mandals across 21 districts had been declared drought-affected after significantly below-normal rainfall and prolonged dry spells, according to Telugu360. The state has already submitted a memorandum seeking central assistance and will furnish a detailed drought report within a week. Naidu also requested that guaranteed employment under the VB-G RAM G scheme be raised to 200 days.

What happens next

The central team told Naidu it will submit its assessment report to the Union Government within 15 days, based on field inspections, discussions with affected farmers and state government data. Central assistance decisions are expected to follow that assessment. For families in the affected districts, the practical position today is unchanged: relief and restoration are being run by the state, and the size and timing of any central package will not be known until the team reports.
